doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

title: Beyond standard notation: the piece En Route
summary: He describes En Route, where musicians carry route cards and move around the stage so the sound moves.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So was standard notation not enough for you in some of your composing? Were there things you wanted instrumentalists to do that really couldn’t be written down in standard notation?

Well yeah, I’ve got pieces like that, yeah, I do. I mean I have pieces, let’s see I could recall “En Route” was like a piece where people had route cards, you know, and with certain instructions that would happen on the route. Like let’s say that you’re on route E, you know, and then I may have a card to say, “Meet you on route E and then establish music with you, and then move on to another part of the composition.” So and that was an interesting composition because you also had the sound moving, you know, the musicians were moving around on the stage to different positions so play en route was one of the instructions. So you would actually have the sound moving across like that.
